from.place: Comparator challenge theorem WeilConjectures.weil_conjectures (lean/Comparator/Weil/Challenge.lean): factorization, functional equation and Riemann hypothesis for smooth proper geometrically integral X over a finite field

title: WeilConjectures.weil_conjectures
statement:
Let k be a finite field with q=#k elements, d a natural number, and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ a morphism of schemes that is smooth of relative dimension d, proper and geometrically integral [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. For a finite field k with q=#k elements, a scheme X and a morphism $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, the zeta series Z(X,t)=f.zetaSeries in Q[[t]] [def-weil-point-counts-zeta] is Z(X,t)=exp(sum_{n>=1} N_n t^n/n), substituted into the formal exponential series, where N_n=f.pointCount n is the number of k-morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}F_{q^n}\to X$ (morphisms g with g followed by f equal to the map induced by $k\to F_{q^n}$), F_{q^n} being the model FiniteField.galoisExtension k n = the splitting field over k of X^{q^n}-X, and N_n=0 (junk value) if this set is infinite. A polynomial with integer coefficients is viewed in Q[[t]] through its coefficientwise image in Q[t] [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map, def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series]. Then there is a family P_0,...,P_{2d} in Z[t] [def-weil-polynomial-ring], indexed by i in {0,...,2d}, with the three properties:
(1) Weil factorization (IsWeilFactorization q d Z P): P_i(0)=1 for every i [def-weil-polynomial-coefficient]; P_0=1-t; P_{2d}=1-q^d t; and Z(X,t) * prod_{i even} P_i = prod_{i odd} P_i in Q[[t]] [def-weil-formal-power-series].
(2) Functional equation (WeilFunctionalEquation q d P): for every i, the multiset of complex roots of P_{2d-i} (roots of its coefficientwise image in C[t], counted with multiplicity) [def-weil-polynomial-root, def-weil-root-multiplicity] equals the image of the multiset of complex roots of P_i under $z\mapsto(q^dz)^{-1}$.
(3) Riemann hypothesis (WeilRiemannHypothesis q d P): for every i and every complex root z of P_i, |z| = q^{-i/2} (real power) [def-weil-complex-absolute-value, def-weil-real-power].
Equivalently the inverse roots alpha of P_i are q^{i/2}-Weil numbers and $\alpha\mapsto q^d/\alpha$ matches the inverse roots of P_i with those of P_{2d-i}.

proof.text: Set $k_0=k$ and $X_0=X$, and choose an algebraic closure $\bar k$ of $k_0$. By def-weil-finite-field-q-elements, $q=p^a$ for a prime $p$ and $a\geq1$, giving the global datum of def-weil-finite-field-fiber. Properness gives separatedness and finite type by def-weil-proper-morphism. For $n\geq1$, lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure (1),(3) identifies $K_n=\{x\in\bar k:x^{q^n}=x\}$ as a subfield containing $k_0$, with $q^n$ elements. The polynomial $h(U)=U^{q^n}-U$ has precisely these $q^n$ roots; since its degree is $q^n$, it splits in $K_n$, and these roots generate $K_n$ as a $k_0$-algebra because they are every element of $K_n$. Apply lem-weil-splitting-field-algebra-equivalence to obtain a $k_0$-algebra isomorphism $e:K_n\simeq h.\mathrm{SplittingField}=E_n$. The induced maps $\operatorname{Spec}(e)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(e^{-1})$ are inverse over $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ by def-weil-affine-spectrum. Sending a point $g:\operatorname{Spec}E_n\to X_0$ to $g\circ\operatorname{Spec}(e^{-1})$ gives the inverse bijections between the two sets of $k_0$-points. Their cardinalities agree, and lem-weil-point-counts-finite (1) makes them finite. Hence the comparator exponential equals the series of def-weil-point-counts-zeta, coefficient by coefficient. Next put $\bar X=X_0\times_{k_0}\bar k$. By lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change this is finite type over $\bar k$. A field has only the ideals $0,1$, so is a Noetherian ring; its one-point affine spectrum is locally Noetherian by pqf-def-locnoeth and is quasi-compact. Thus lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian makes $\bar X$ Noetherian, in particular locally Noetherian. By lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence (1), $\bar X\to\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$. Its only fibre is $\bar X$, so def-sbc-smooth-morphisms gives local topological dimension $d$ at every point. Apply lem-sbc-constant-local-dimension-components with $Y=O=\bar X$: every irreducible component has dimension $d$. This is the pure-dimension clause of def-weil-geometric-hypotheses. For every extension $k_0\to k^{\prime}$, geometrical integrality (def-pc-geometrically-irreducible) makes $(X_0)_{k^{\prime}}$ integral; lem-pc-integral-scheme-irreducible makes it nonempty and irreducible, and lem-pc-irreducible-space-connected makes it connected. Thus $X_0$ is geometrically connected without needing a separate closure criterion. All hypotheses of def-weil-smooth-proper-datum and the final Weil component theorems are now verified.

proof.text: Apply thm-weil-final-integrality to this datum, obtaining the same family $P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$ for $0\leq i\leq2d$, with $P_i(0)=1$ and $Z=\prod_iP_i^{(-1)^{i+1}}$ in $\mathbf Q(T)$. Use def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map along $\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Q$; put $A=\prod_{i\text{ odd}}P_i$ and $B=\prod_{i\text{ even}}P_i$ in $\mathbf Q[T]$. Both have constant term $1$. The displayed rational factorization says $Z=A/B$. By def-weil-rational-power-series, its expansion at zero agrees with the point-count series; by def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series, $B(0)=1$ makes $B$ a unit in $\mathbf Q[[T]]$, so this identity is exactly $ZB=A$ in $\mathbf Q[[T]]$. The two endpoint identities $P_0=1-T$ and $P_{2d}=1-q^dT$ follow from thm-weil-final-betti for these same factors. Reindexing by $\operatorname{Fin}(2d+1)$ sends $i$ to the factor $P_i$ and preserves parity. The coefficient and product conventions of def-weil-polynomial-coefficient, def-weil-polynomial-ring and def-weil-formal-power-series then give every field of IsWeilFactorization for this one family.

source.place: Clause (i) and Clause (ii): factorization and the identification of the canonical factors

proof.text: For this same family, prop-duality-reciprocity gives $b_i=b_{2d-i}$ and the identity $P_{2d-i}(q^{-d}T^{-1})=(-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}D_i^{-1}P_i(T)$ in $\mathbf Q[T,T^{-1}]$. Applying $\mathbf Q\to\mathbf C$ to its finitely many coefficients preserves the identity, by the coefficientwise ring-map convention. Here $D_i$ is nonzero because $P_i(0)=1$ makes $P_i$ nonzero and $D_i$ is its signed leading coefficient. Fix a root $\beta$ of $P_i$ in $\mathbf C$. By lem-weil-reciprocal-root-factorization it is nonzero. Set $c=q^{-d}$ and $\gamma=c/\beta=(q^d\beta)^{-1}$. Write $P_{2d-i}(U)=(U-\gamma)^mR(U)$ with $R(\gamma)\neq0$; this is the multiplicity definition, also allowing $m=0$. Then $c/T-\gamma=-\gamma(T-\beta)/T$, so $P_{2d-i}(c/T)=(-\gamma/T)^m(T-\beta)^mR(c/T)$. At $T=\beta$, the factors $-\gamma/T$ and $R(c/T)$ are nonzero, so its order is exactly $m$. The other side of the Laurent identity is a factor nonzero at $\beta$ times $P_i(T)$, and therefore has exactly the multiplicity of $\beta$ in $P_i$. These multiplicities are equal. The transformation $\beta\mapsto c/\beta$ is an involution on $\mathbf C^\times$; exchanging $i$ and $2d-i$ gives the converse for every root. Thus the complex root multisets correspond with multiplicity, exactly WeilFunctionalEquation, with $i.\mathrm{rev}$ corresponding to $2d-i$. Constant factors have empty root multiset, and the same identity handles them.

source.place: Clause (v): degreewise Laurent reciprocity, read as the complex-root functional equation in clause (2) of the updated main-20261015 statement; explicit reflection and multiplicity calculation supplied here.

proof.text: Use lem-weil-pbc-relative-algebraic-closure-algclosed with $F=\mathbf Q$ and $\Omega=\mathbf C$. It gives the algebraic closure $A=\{z\in\mathbf C:z\text{ algebraic over }\mathbf Q\}$ as an actual subfield of $\mathbf C$. Instantiate thm-weil-final-rh with this choice of $\overline{\mathbf Q}=A$, which does not alter the integral factors. Let $z$ be any complex root of $P_i$. Its constant coefficient is $1$, so $P_i$ is nonzero, and the equation $P_i(z)=0$ with rational coefficients says exactly that $z$ is algebraic over $\mathbf Q$. Thus it gives an element $\beta\in A$ whose inclusion in $\mathbf C$ is $z$. Evaluating the finite coefficient sum in the subfield $A$ shows $P_i(\beta)=0$: its image under the injective inclusion is $P_i(z)=0$. By lem-weil-reciprocal-root-factorization, $\beta\neq0$ and it is the ordinary root corresponding to a reciprocal root. The restriction of $A\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$ to $\mathbf Q(\beta)$ is an embedding $\tau$ with $\tau(\beta)=z$. The ordinary-root clause of thm-weil-final-rh gives $|z|=|\tau(\beta)|=q^{-i/2}$. By def-weil-polynomial-root, def-weil-complex-absolute-value and def-weil-real-power, this is precisely WeilRiemannHypothesis for all complex roots of the same family. Together with steps 2 and 3 it gives the three required properties simultaneously.

theorem weil_conjectures (d : ℕ) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] [IsProper f]
    [GeometricallyIntegral f] :
    ∃ P : Fin (2 * d + 1) → Polynomial ℤ,
      IsWeilFactorization (Nat.card k) d f.zetaSeries P ∧
      WeilFunctionalEquation (Nat.card k) d P ∧
      WeilRiemannHypothesis (Nat.card k) d P
